title: Status page transparency upgrades — working notes (taxonomy, mapping edge cases, links)
content:
Doc intent: messy working notes for the “Status page transparency upgrades” project. This is NOT the final taxonomy/spec; it’s where we dump ideas, edge cases, and links to incidents/support feedback.

Last reviewed in working session w/ Product + Support (notes from 2024-06-28). Owner for next cleanup pass: Christine.

---

1) Problem statements (from customers + Support)

- “Status page says API degraded but we only saw streaming failures.” (SUP-18421)
  - Customers don’t know if they should fall back to non-streaming, retry, or switch model/region.
- “Which region is impacted?” (SUP-18502)
  - Current components are too global; partial regional issues look like platform-wide outages.
- “Can you send a post-incident timeline?” (SUP-18455)
  - Enterprise expects a summary + timeline even if impact is partial and root cause is provider-related.
- Support asks for consistent macro language that matches SRE status updates (INT-990)

Takeaway: component granularity must match customer decision points:
- streaming vs non-streaming
- embeddings/rerank separate from chat/generation
- region scoping (us-east/us-west/eu-west)
- Dedicated/Private control plane vs Hosted API

---

2) Brainstorm: customer-facing component list (draft)

Naming principle: customer-comprehensible, avoid internal service names.

Top-level (candidate) components:

A) Hosted API
- API Gateway (auth, request acceptance, rate limiting, request routing)
- Text Generation (non-streaming) — “Responses”
- Streaming (SSE/WebSocket streaming responses)
- Embeddings
- Rerank
- Batch/Async Jobs (if we expose this) — open question
- Model Catalog / Model Availability (only if we can represent model-family pinning issues clearly)
- Capacity & Routing (this is the “scheduler” debate; see Slack eng-sre thread_1719075544_009812)

B) Console
- Console UI
- Console APIs (if split is helpful; otherwise one component)

C) Dedicated
- Dedicated Control Plane (provisioning, scaling controls, quotas, keys)
- Dedicated Serving (data plane) — might be region scoped per customer? tricky.

D) Private
- Private Control Plane (customer VPC control plane)
- Private On‑prem Package (only if we can support it consistently; else keep under Private)

E) Core platform shared dependencies (only if they have distinct customer-visible failure modes)
- Auth & API Keys (if separate from API Gateway; careful not to leak auth specifics)
- Billing/Usage Reporting (probably not on status page unless it causes customer impact)

Region subcomponents (Hosted API serving)
- Hosted API — us-east
- Hosted API — us-west
- Hosted API — eu-west

Question: do we want regional components per route (Streaming us-east) or keep region under a single Hosted API region component?
- Current leaning: region components for Serving and separate global components for feature surfaces (Streaming/Embeddings/Rerank) only when failure mode is feature-specific.

---

3) Quick mapping rules (draft, to be moved into mapping guidelines)

Rule 1: Prefer smallest customer-actionable component.
- If only Streaming is failing (disconnects/timeouts), mark Streaming degraded, not “API Gateway” or “Hosted API”.
- If requests never get accepted / widespread 429/5xx before routing, mark API Gateway.

Rule 2: Don’t mark more than ~3 components unless truly necessary.
- Over-marking makes everything look broken.

Rule 3: If impact is region-scoped, reflect it.
- If elevated errors only in us-east, mark Hosted API — us-east (and optionally the specific feature component if it’s feature-limited).

Rule 4: Model-family incidents
- If specific model family is unavailable but platform is otherwise healthy:
  - Option A: mark “Model Availability” component degraded.
  - Option B: mark the route component + include affected models in incident body.
- Concern: new “Model Availability” component might confuse customers if they don’t use model pinning.
- Tentative: keep as “Text Generation” + mention models by name in incident update; revisit once we see frequency.

Rule 5: Dedicated vs Hosted
- Dedicated capacity incident: do not mark Hosted API components unless cross-cutting.
- If control plane is broken but serving still works, mark Dedicated Control Plane (not Dedicated Serving).

Rule 6: Private
- For Private deployments, we may have limited visibility and comms constraints.
- Public status page should only reflect Redwood-operated systems, not customer-managed networks.
- Use language like: “We are investigating reports from some Private deployments” vs stating specific customer environments.

---

4) Edge cases / scenario notes (needs examples in runbook)

4.1 Streaming-only failures (most common mismatch today)
Signals:
- Streaming disconnects increase
- Keepalive timeouts
- Non-streaming completion requests succeed
Status mapping:
- Component: Streaming
- Impact language: “Some streaming responses may disconnect or terminate early; non-streaming requests are not impacted.”
Customer actions:
- Suggest retries with exponential backoff; optionally switch to non-streaming temporarily.
Links:
- Support: SUP-18421
- Incident review thread: Slack incidents/thread_1719459871_883120

4.2 Elevated 429s due to capacity constraints (not total outage)
Signals:
- 429 rate up; increased queue time / throttling
- Often region + model specific
Status mapping:
- Component: Capacity & Routing OR Hosted API — <region> (need decision)
- If it manifests only for one model family, include in text: “Model X/Y affected”
Customer actions:
- Retry with jittered backoff; use fallback model; region pinning guidance
Notes:
- Avoid saying “scheduler” (internal jargon)

4.3 Partial embedding degradation
Signals:
- Embedding p95 latency up; success rate still high
Status mapping:
- Component: Embeddings
- Impact: “Degraded performance (higher latency) for embeddings requests”
Customer actions:
- Increase client timeout; batch where possible

4.4 Console vs API mismatch
- Console shows errors/blank pages but inference is healthy
Status mapping:
- Component: Console
- Don’t mark API Gateway unless console API calls share same failure mechanism

4.5 Provider networking incident (cloud region issue)
- We can say “upstream provider networking issue” but avoid vendor-specific sensitive details.
Status mapping:
- Component: Hosted API — affected region
- Impact language should be specific (latency, errors, streaming disconnects)
Notes:
- This will matter for post-incident summaries: root cause category should be “Upstream provider dependency” not “AWS <specific internal service>”.

4.6 Degraded performance vs partial outage
- Need consistency with SLO burn and customer impact classifier.
- Use “Degraded performance” when success rate mostly OK but latency elevated.
- Use “Partial outage” when a meaningful % of requests fail and workarounds may exist.

---

5) Open questions

- Regional component strategy
  - Do we create separate components: “Streaming — us-east” etc? Potential component explosion.
  - Alternative: region-specific Serving components + feature components only when issue is feature-specific across regions.

- “Capacity & Routing” component naming
  - Pros: explains 429s/queueing; customer-actionable.
  - Cons: ambiguous; may attract blame for any latency spike.
  - Options: “Capacity & Routing”, “Capacity Management”, “Request Routing”.

- Model availability representation
  - Is a dedicated “Model Availability” component worth it?
  - We must avoid implying all models have identical SLAs.

- How to represent Dedicated customer-specific incidents
  - Public status page is global. Dedicated incidents can affect one customer only.
  - Proposal: only use public status for Dedicated when >=2 customers or shared Dedicated control plane is affected; otherwise handle via direct comms.
  - Need policy confirmation w/ CS sponsor (Jasmine) + disclosure approvers.

---

6) Draft “definition of done” for taxonomy/mapping work (rough)

- Component list finalized + definitions written in plain language.
- For each component:
  - 2–3 example failure modes
  - What customers observe
  - Typical mitigations/workarounds we can safely recommend
  - Primary internal signals/alerts backing it
- Mapping guidelines include:
  - single vs multiple components
  - region scoping rules
  - model-family mention guidance
  - Dedicated/Private disclosure boundaries

---

7) Links / breadcrumbs (for whoever is writing the formal Confluence pages)

Support + customer feedback
- SUP-18421 — streaming-only but status said “API degraded”
- SUP-18455 — request for post-incident timeline/summary
- SUP-18502 — confusion about region scoping
- INT-990 — Support macro request

Internal coordination threads
- Kickoff/owner alignment: Slack eng-oncall/thread_1718891023_441120
- Taxonomy naming debate (“scheduler” vs “Capacity & Routing”): Slack eng-sre/thread_1719075544_009812
- Real-time comms review (component selection + wording): Slack incidents/thread_1719453320_601299
- Streaming vs API component decision example: Slack incidents/thread_1719459871_883120

Project tracking
- Linear epic: ENG-4821
- Components impl: ENG-4822, ENG-4823
- Incident-bot prompts/sync: ENG-4824, ENG-4825
- Post-incident summary workflow: ENG-4826

---

8) TODO (next 1–2 weeks)

- [Christine] Consolidate component list + propose final names for Design review (DES-211)
- [Aisha Bello] Identify metrics/signals we trust per component; flag gaps (tie into signal coverage audit)
- [Tomáš] Draft 5 scenario examples for runbook (streaming-only, 429 capacity, embeddings latency, console-only, region-specific 5xx)
- [Rafael] Draft mapping guidelines v0 + share with Support for feedback
- [Talia] Confirm disclosure boundaries for Dedicated/Private + “provider issue” wording with approvers

Notes to self:
- Keep taxonomy stable over time; use aliases/redirects if we rename components later.
- Avoid overpromising: status page guidance must not read like an SLA guarantee.
